bull_bear.body: INR137.81cr (53%) of INR259.32cr IPO proceeds utilized; capex prioritized for capacity expansion; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on debt-free growth via internal accruals and IPO funds
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Steel price volatility (20% increase); export freight surcharges (up to $2,000/container); forex risk (rupee depreciation to INR94.78/$); Iran conflict impacting logistics; labor shortages in Q1; monsoon disruption in Q2; order closure delays in US due to inflation; 15-20% raw material exposure unhedged
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on top-line growth (25% guidance), cautious on margins due to uncontrollable inputs; optimistic on export potential post-tariff cut; transparent on supply chain disruptions; avoiding margin guidance until stability returns; emphasis on disciplined execution and capacity utilization
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Sanand is India’s only PEB plant with AISC and CWB certifications — critical for US/Canada access; 80-85% raw material hedging via firm orders/inventory is industry standard but 15-20% open exposure caused INR6cr forex+steel loss; export revenue recognition delayed by shipping timelines (Feb 12 cutoff deferred Q4 revenue to Q1FY27); data centre opportunity is nascent but massive (12K-15K tons/project); no steel hedging possible in India — only inventory-based mitigation
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds utilisation as on June 30, 2026: Net Amount Received Rs 259.32 cr, Amount Utilised Rs 146.69 cr (56.57%), Pending to be Utilized Rs 112.64 cr - split as Prepayment of Term Loan Rs 58.75 cr (100.00% utilised), Capital Expenditure Rs 135.78 cr (17.49% utilised, Rs 112.03 cr pending) and General Corporate Purpose Rs 64.79 cr (99.06% utilised).
- Net Debt to Equity (times) is charted as 0.69, 0.82, 0.88, 0.61, 0.12 against FY22-FY26; tangible net worth rose to Rs 657.10 cr in FY26 from Rs 306.53 cr in FY25, and equity share capital to Rs 57.15 cr from Rs 50.00 cr.
- Cash flow footnote: the audited FY26 accounts show Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities of negative Rs 30.88 Cr "due to inclusion of Usage of funds to the tune of Rs. 120.81 Cr on account of Bank Fixed Deposits earmarked for IPO objects"; the deck presents an "Adjusted" cash flow reclassifying this to investing, so "Recalculating Net Cash flow from Operating activities will hence change from negative cash flow of Rs. 30.88 Cr to positive cash flow of Rs. 89.93 Cr." Both readings are the deck's own.
- The company listed on NSE & BSE in 2025 ("Entered India's Capital Markets through Listing on NSE & BSE").
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Phenix: FY26 revenue INR985cr (+29%), export revenue INR166cr (+156% YoY), volume 73,000 tons (7,045 tons exported); Sanand plant capacity: 72,000 tons, expanding to 92,000 tons by Q2FY27; Cheyyar plant: 50-55% utilization in FY26, targeting 68-70% in FY27; Proflex: FY26 revenue INR275cr (+23%), installed area 20.3M sqm, capacity to increase by 200,000 sqm/yr with 3 new units (1 commissioned, 2 to be commissioned Q2FY27)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Two-division structure: Phenix - "PEBs & complex structural steel components" with FY26 Revenue from Operations of Rs 985 cr - and Proflex - "Self supported steel roofing solutions" with FY26 Revenue from Operations of Rs 275 cr; consolidated FY26 Revenue from Operations is stated as Rs 1,260 cr.
- "Sanand facility: India's only PEB manufacturing unit with certification from American Institute of Steel Construction and Canadian Welding Bureau Registration." The facilities slide repeats this as "Only PEB manufacturing facility in India with both certifications - AISC & CWB" for Sanand, while Cheyyar is shown as a "PEB manufacturing facility in India with a certification from AISC".
- "Operations span 23 countries across multiple geographies including US, Canada, Brazil, South Africa, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Nigeria, Kenya and Seychelles", supported by a wholly owned subsidiary Phenix Construction Technologies Inc. in the USA (established 2017) and a marketing head office in Ahmedabad.
- "2,000+ customer groups served pan-India; repeat customers contributed 54.07% of FY26 consolidated operating revenue", with a "Relationship of >15 years with some customers"; the repeat-customer chart shows 66%, 73%, 57%, 54% against FY23-FY26.
- Track record slides cite Phenix at "18 Years of operations", "Over 1,700 Projects" and "Over 7,30,000 MT Installed till date"; Proflex at "24 Years of operations", "Over 8,700 Projects" and "Over 2.07 Cr Sq. m. Installed till date" ("# As on 31st March 2026").
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Guidance] "From growth Prospective, we remain confident of delivering revenue growth of over 25% in FY 27" - Malav Patel, Jt. Managing Director.
- [Order book] "Orders on Hand stood at Rs 1,053 crore, representing a 25% YoY growth. Proflex division accounted for 20.5% (Rs 216 crore). Phenix division accounted for 79.5% (Rs 837 crore). Within the Phenix division, export orders were Rs 278 crore, bulk of which to be shipped during the current Fiscal." Orders on hand are shown with a "4Y CAGR: 24.1% (FY22-FY26)".
- [Market size - Crisil/Allied source] "With a projected CAGR of ~10%, the global PEB market is expected to reach USD 32-35 billion by 2029, while the Indian market, growing slightly faster, is expected to reach INR 330-345 billion by 2030" (from INR 210 Bn in FY25E, "CAGR: 10-15%"); the self-supported roofing market is "expected to reach USD 0.87-0.92 billion by 2029" globally and "INR 3.8-4.2 billion by 2030" in India (CAGR ~3-4%).
- [Industry structure] "Large, organised players grow at faster clip than overall pre-engineered steel building industry" (chart compares "Industry CAGR FY19-FY25" with "Top 7 Players CAGR FY20-FY24"); demand drivers cited include industrial capex reaching "INR 7.1 Tn by Fiscal 2030, marking an average annual increase of 1.6x", the National Steel Policy, PLI for specialty steel, warehousing/cold storage expansion and railway investment.
- [Management] Promoter-led board with two Joint Managing Directors (Chirag Hasmukhbhai Patel, Malav Girishbhai Patel); divisional CEOs Mayur Satishbhai Patel (Proflex, CEO since Feb 2006) and Pankaj Naresh (Phenix); CFO Keyur Bachubhai Shah (with the company since 2007, CFO since April 2024); Non-Executive Chairman & Independent Director Hemant Ishwarlal Modi, former Vice Chairman & MD of JMC Projects.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin: 11.9% (vs 14% YoY); FY26 margin: 12.5% (vs 13.6%); forex loss: INR3.9cr in Q4, INR6.04cr in FY26; steel prices up 20% domestically; export freight costs surged due to war; adjusted EBITDA margin (ex-forex): 13% in Q4 and FY26; export EBITDA margin: 16-17% vs domestic: 10-11%
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 25% YoY; margin: no guidance due to steel/freight/forex volatility; order inflow: expected to remain strong with INR1,100cr+ pipeline; capex/commissioning: INR100cr in FY27 (Sanand expansion Q2FY27, Cheyyar capex H2FY27)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR1,083cr as of March 31, 2026 (Phenix: INR871cr, Proflex: INR212cr); export portion: INR279cr (32% of total); new orders: INR73.18cr (March 2026) and INR71.95cr (April 2026) domestic PEB orders
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Data centre construction (estimated 12,000-15,000 tons PEB per project); potential INR50,000-60,000 tons pipeline under evaluation; export market expansion into Canada (CWB certified); Cheyyar plant ramp-up to serve South India demand
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: M&B Engineering delivered strong 27% revenue growth and 35% order book expansion in FY26, driven by export surge and capacity investments, but margins were pressured by forex losses, steel inflation, and war-related logistics costs; the 25% US tariff cut and 20,000-ton Sanand expansion position the company for sustained export-led growth in FY27 despite near-term cost headwinds.

meta.thesis: M&B Engineering delivered strong 27% revenue growth and 35% order book expansion in FY26, driven by export surge and capacity investments, but margins were pressured by forex losses, steel inflation, and war-related logistics costs; the 25% US tariff cut and 20,000-ton Sanand expansion position the company for sustained export-led growth in FY27 despite near-term cost headwinds.
